title: Coast Guard responds to two search and rescue cases as Hurricane Irma approaches
description: Crewmembers aboard an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter from Coast Guard Air Station Clearwater rescue two boaters and their dog 100 miles south of Apalachicola, Florida, Sunday, Sept. 10, 2017. The boaters, aboard the sailboat Magnolia Wind, alerted the Coast Guard after loosing steering while en route for Mississippi to avoid Hurricane Irma. (U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Andrew Barresi)
keywords: AIR STATION CLEARWATER, Jayhawk helicopter, Coast Guard rescue swimmer, Andrew Barresi, Hurricane Irma, Irma, Coast Guard, C-130, USCG, Hurricane

transcript.text: ^- Last night, around 10 o'clock, I was notified
^that we would be launching for a disabled sailing vessel
approximately 120 miles west of Sarasota, Florida.
We ended up launching a little bit
after 11 o'clock last night, local time
and flew directly to the last known position
of the disabled sailing boat, which was just
in the beginning bands of Hurricane Irma.
We arrived on scene, located the vessel,
and we vectored a Coast Guard H-60 helicopter from Mobile
on scene, and they were able to successfully hoist
four survivors from that boat.
After that case, we diverted to another
disabled sailing vessel approximately at 100 miles south
of Apalachicola, Florida, and another H-60 crew
from Clearwater, which is deployed here
to New Orleans, was sent to that case.
^- It was definitely one of the more difficult cases
^that I've been on.
I got into the water, and it was
about a 40 knot wind with 20 to 25 foot seas,
which were pretty big.
I approached the vessel.
Took a little bit of work,
but I climbed on board, made sure everybody was safe
and accounted for, made sure there were no injuries.
Everybody had their proper flotation,
and then one by one we jumped off the ship
and I towed each survivor to safety
and then with the second survivor,
we brought the dog with us.
^- [Louis] C-130 located us.
^Helicopter, rescue diver, rescue swimmers came down,
swam, got us, we hopped in the water
and he took us individually back to the helicopter
and back here, and our little dog, too.
Thank God for the Coast Guard.
